story: On Magnolia Loop this sunny Thursday afternoon, Gary sits content as Rosa heads off to the store, reassuring her he'll eat whatever she cooks for Friday's cornbread. Donna is eager to get Gary onto the pickleball court tomorrow, while Hal, satisfied with his review of Gary's paperwork, confirms the filing is clean and asks Rosa about allergies. Rosa, cheerful as ever, checks with Hal before she leaves, since she'd rather know his food preferences now than at the stove.

gary.thought_process: Hal's got my paperwork and said he'll read every line against L-01 before I file, so the ball's in his court. Donna's moving her flamingos, Rosa's heading to the store for Friday. Rosa asked if anybody can't eat something, and nobody's answered for me. I'm bringing cornbread, no restrictions on my end, and a quick answer helps her shop. I shouldn't re-ask Hal about the paperwork. Keep it short, thank Rosa, and let the others get on with their afternoon.

parameters.content: Nothing I can't eat, Rosa, so shop however you like. I'll have the cornbread there Friday, still warm if I time it right.

donna.thought_process: Gary just handed his cart-and-lights application to Hal, Rosa's off to shop for Friday, and Hal says he'll count my flamingos. I already told the flock to move the extras around back, so the Hal promise is handled. My real goal is getting Gary onto the pickleball ladder with me, and he's lit up about his paddle and first practice. Court reservations max out at 2 hours (L-05), so I can pin down a time now. Rosa and Hal have heard enough from me already, so I'll turn to Gary, keep it short, and lock in his practice before Friday dinner.

parameters.content: Gary, once Hal's done with your paperwork, let's get you on the court tomorrow before Rosa's dinner. I'll book two hours, that's the limit, and we'll start with the basics so you can partner with me for the ladder.

hal.thought_process: Gary handed me his form and it's clean: lights and sound both listed, ten o'clock cutoff written in, lights held until Thanksgiving. That squares with L-01, L-03 and L-04. Donna says she's moving the extras out back, so the flamingo count should land at three from the street. My original goal was to report them, but both are cooperating, and a neighborhood runs on people checking each other's work, not on turning each other in. Rosa's about to head to the store and asked about allergies. Nobody has answered her yet, and I'm the only one with a reply. I'll give Gary his verdict first, then let him know I'll be counting flamingos on my way home.

parameters.content: I've read it against L-01, Gary, and it's clean: lights, sound, cutoff, all in order. File it as written. And Rosa, no allergies here, I'll eat whatever's put in front of me.

rosa.thought_process: I already told Gary I'm headed to the store for Friday's dinner, and I asked everybody to flag food restrictions. Hal and Gary are busy with the cart paperwork and Donna's on her flamingos, so nobody's answered the food question yet. I shouldn't repeat my whole invite. Hal's the one I haven't heard a dietary word from, and I'd rather ask him directly now than discover a problem at the stove on Friday. Quick, blunt, warm, then I get to the store.

parameters.content: Hal, before you bury yourself in that form, anything you can't or won't eat on Friday? I'm leaving for the store in a minute and I'd rather know now than at the stove.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
